summary: Both edits carry every intent requirement and match each other in content. Both add a concrete type signature and file locations that the intent leaves to 'the interface'. In chain, the booking-repository change is placed on a model node whose only file is schema.prisma.

findings.detail: The intent only says 'the optional `{ category, details }` object described in the interface' and 'the chainable `withAssignmentReason` builder method'. The note fixes the exact types: 'assignmentReason?: { category: string; details?: string | null } | null' and 'withAssignmentReason(assignmentReason?: { category: string; details?: string | null } | null)'. Making details optional and nullable, and the whole value nullable, are decisions the intent does not spell out.

The note and node name files the intent never mentions: '`CalendarEvent` in `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`', 'packages/features/CalendarEventBuilder.ts', and, on assignment-reason-category, 'packages/features/bookings/lib/getAssignmentReasonCategory.ts'. The intent names only the function and the builder method, not where they live.

'Fetch both the reason enum and detailed reason string in the booking repository' is placed on model-booking, whose only file is packages/prisma/schema.prisma. In the chain graph, packages/features/bookings/repositories/ belongs to handle-new-booking, so the repository change happens there. This is a small placement doubt, since model-booking is still a reasonable conceptual home. Fresh is fine: its booking-model lists BookingRepository.ts.
